title: RIA sets out five rail supply sector ‘asks’ of government ahead of the October budget

The Railway Industry Association has published its five priorities for the government’s budget on October 28, saying its proposals would support ambitions for a strong rail network in an era of constrained public finances.

RIA’s five main ‘asks’ are:

‘The October budget needs to recognise that demand for rail is growing and to set out how we invest now to provide the resilience and capacity the government needs for a safe and durable railway in future’, said RIA Chief Executive Darren Caplan on September 10.

‘A clear, joined-up investment strategy which brings together government, Great British Railways, devolved and regional authorities, and the supply sector, will deliver for passengers and freight customers a safe and resilient railway, while supporting the jobs and economic growth the government wants and the country needs.’

Rail Business UK provides editorially independent and industry-focused coverage of the British rail industry, including operations, infrastructure and the supply sector.

The rail freight sector has welcomed Secretary of State for Transport Heidi Alexander’s announcement of a target to increase tonne-km 40% by 2040, with operators calling on the government to work with them to create the conditions needed to achieve this growth.

The Scottish government is to bring arm’s-length agency Transport Scotland under direct control as part of a programme of public sector reforms being implemented by the ruling Scottish National Party.

The Chartered Institution of Railway Operators has published a policy paper offering what it terms ‘practical recommendations’ to help ensure the UK’s rail reform delivers a railway that is both locally empowered and nationally coherent.

The RMT trade union has rejected a proposal to introduce what it sees as Driver Only Operation on East West Rail services.
